primary_diagnosis: Diabetic Kidney Disease (progressive diabetic nephropathy, CKD stage 3b)
clinical_reasoning_summary: The patient’s long‑standing type 2 diabetes, obesity, and hypertension have produced classic diabetic nephropathy evidenced by elevated creatinine, reduced eGFR, and nephrotic‑range proteinuria. Untreated hypertension (including likely masked nocturnal hypertension) and untreated obstructive sleep apnea act as major accelerants of renal decline. CKD‑related anemia, possible overtreatment of diabetes, and metabolic syndrome‑related liver disease further complicate the picture. Gaps in guideline‑directed therapy (absence of ACE‑I/ARB, SGLT2‑i, statin, CPAP) explain ongoing disease progression. Additional contributors such as subclinical atherosclerosis, asymptomatic bacteriuria, CKD‑mineral‑bone disorder, and psychosocial stress are included as lower‑probability diagnoses.

recommended_workup: 24‑hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring to detect masked nocturnal hypertension
Urine albumin‑to‑creatinine ratio and repeat urine protein quantification
Urine culture with sensitivity to evaluate pyuria
Complete blood count with iron studies, reticulocyte count, haptoglobin, LDH to characterize anemia and rule out hemolysis
Comprehensive liver panel (AST, ALT, ALP, GGT, total and direct bilirubin) and abdominal ultrasound or FibroScan for NAFLD/NASH
Serum calcium, phosphate, PTH, and 25‑OH vitamin D for CKD‑MBD assessment
Full lipid panel and calculation of ASCVD 10‑year risk; consider coronary calcium scoring or stress testing
Polysomnography repeat or CPAP adherence assessment; initiate CPAP if not already prescribed
Medication reconciliation and pharmacy refill review to assess insulin dosing appropriateness; consider adding SGLT2‑i or GLP‑1 RA
Standardized mental‑health screening (PHQ‑9, GAD‑7) and referral for counseling or social support services
